### What problem does this PR solve?

Issue Number: close https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/issues/26580, https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/issues/28058

Drop table with placement policy or direct placement options should clean PD about the rules.

issue_context.title: Support named PLACEMENT POLICY
issue_context.body:
This is a sub-task of Placement Rules in SQL: https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/issues/18030

Support the ability to `CREATE PLACEMENT POLICY` with the same options available in `CREATE TABLE|ALTER TABLE` context.

The following subtasks are known:

* [x] Parser: {CREATE|ALTER} PLACEMENT POLICY placement_options https://github.com/pingcap/parser/pull/1313
* [x] Parser: SHOW CREATE PLACEMENT POLICY x, DROP PLACEMENT POLICY [IF EXISTS] x; https://github.com/pingcap/parser/pull/1295 https://github.com/pingcap/parser/pull/1298
* [x] Design table in mysql.* for persisting placement policies. https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/pull/27251
* [x] Ensure {CREATE|ALTER|DROP} PLACEMENT POLICY requires the PLACEMENT_ADMIN privilege https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/issues/27603
* [x] #27714
* [x] ALTER PLACEMENT POLICY should update placement rules for all tables in scope in PD.
* [x] DROP PLACEMENT POLICY should clear the placement rules for all tables in scope in PD, and reset the `SHOW CREATE TABLE` info to no longer have the placement policy named.
comments:
I have moved the tasks of this sub-issue to https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/issues/18030

This was a suggestion to make it easier to see what tasks are unassigned. It makes sense to me, so I am going to close this issue.

review_comments:
I'm not very understand what is the case testing for. I think dependency is a computed value, so if the table will not exists after dropping, it can be guaranteed relationship is right.

Maybe `getPlacementPolicyDependedObjectsIDs` is what we really want to test?

I just want to make it explicit by fetching it up and and say: "look! there 2 tables depend on that policy"

Otherwise, it's kind of black box handled by ddl interface. the logic is same like `getPlacementPolicyDependedObjectsIDs`

It seems we use the object id as the rule id when creating it. Is it better to make a more semantic names like `pl_tb_1` ? `pl` is short for 'placement rule' and `tb_1` stands for it is a rule group for table with id 1. It may be easier to maintain and distinguish from other rules created by others.
However, It is not the work for current pr. May be we can discuss it in the weekly meeting.
you means the group_id? yes it's kind of customized format, we can talk about it to make it sense
Why not generating the default bundle using the schema's meta.

yes we can, copyed from wanghe's work for simplicity.
cases is that: once schema did not set a policy, here may need a default bundle with `PDBundleID` (also from cache or via http to pd). 

cache problem may be your concern, I will change this when all to-do things are much more clear.

If `part. PlacementPolicyRef == nil` but `tblInfo.PlacementPolicyRef.ID == policy.ID` partition should also depend on the policy.

In the design doc: https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/master/docs/design/2020-06-24-placement-rules-in-sql.md#partitioned-tables

> The semantics of partitioning are different to the default database policy. When a table is partitioned, the partitions will by default inherit the same placement policy as the table.

yes, the inherit work haven't been done yet.
(table inherit db, partition inherit table, and some other details should be dig out. I will do it in next PR)
